cases.name: repo_is_findable
cases.why: the ask names "my Annoy-DataSync project" and no id, so finding it is the first thing either arm does. Worth a case of its own because a search that answers `total_count: 0` for a repository that exists does not look like a broken fixture -- it looks like an agent concluding there is nothing there, which is what one draw of the MCP arm did for 48 requests and 1.2M tokens before giving up.

cases.name: namespace_is_listable
cases.why: the ask names two datasets and no ids, so enumerating the account is the first thing an arm does -- and it is the operation that cost this task a draw. Both of the MCP arm's opening operations, `ls hf://datasets/<owner> --limit 100` and `search hf://datasets "Annoy" --limit 50`, were refused by the fake with a sentence telling it the URI was malformed, and it reported the repositories unavailable. strukto-ai/mirage#982 serves both. The mirage arm enumerates through its mount rather than its CLI because the `hf` it is given has no listing subcommand, so `/hub` is where its view of the namespace lives; that is the comparison, not a normalisation of one

cases.name: issue_body
cases.why: the ask is a reply to this issue, so both arms have to see the same one

cases.name: raw_card_names_its_source
cases.why: the raw dataset's card is where the trail to HuggingFaceTB starts; if the two arms read a different card they are answering different questions

cases.name: source_card_license
cases.why: the answer itself, read off a repository neither arm is pointed at -- `hf_fs` on one side, `hf download` on the other. This is the case that would fail if either arm could only see what it was mounted.

mirage.command: hf download HuggingFaceTB/smollm-corpus README.md --repo-type dataset --local-dir /tmp/src >/dev/null && head -c 200 /tmp/src/README.md

cases.name: model_card_license
cases.why: the other source, and a model rather than a dataset -- the kind is a URI segment on one arm (`hf_fs` accepts hf://<kind>/<namespace>/<name> and nothing else) and a flag defaulting to `model` on the other, so getting it wrong reads as a missing repository rather than a wrong answer

mirage.command: hf download deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2.5 README.md --repo-type model --local-dir /tmp/mdl >/dev/null && head -c 200 /tmp/mdl/README.md

cases.name: linked_model_license
cases.why: the model card declares `license: other` and points to this document, whose derivative-use conditions are needed to compare it with ODC-BY. The exact URL from the pinned card is served from one frozen capture to both arms.

mcp.pipe: grep -o 'downstream derivative versions of the model could be released under different licensing terms' | head -1

mirage.pipe: grep -o 'downstream derivative versions of the model could be released under different licensing terms' | head -1
